sanskrit: atha karṇāstram astreṇa pratihatyārjunaḥ svayam diśaḥ khaṃ caiva bhūmiṃ ca prāvṛṇoc charavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then Arjuna, having himself beaten back Karṇa's missile with a counter-missile, blanketed the quarters, the sky, and the earth with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: musalānīva niṣpetuḥ parighā iva ceṣavaḥ śataghnya iva cāpy anye vajrāṇy ugrāṇi vāpare
english: Some of his arrows fell like maces, others like iron bludgeons, others again like śataghnīs, and still others like fierce thunderbolts.

sanskrit: tair vadhyamānaṃ tat sainyaṃ sapattyaśvarathadvipam nimīlitākṣam atyartham udabhrāmyat samantataḥ
english: Slaughtered by those shafts, that host with its foot-soldiers, horses, chariots, and elephants reeled about in every direction, its eyes shut tight in utter distress.

sanskrit: niṣkaivalyaṃ tadā yuddhaṃ prāpur aśvanaradvipāḥ vadhyamānāḥ śarair anye tadā bhītāḥ pradudruvuḥ
english: Horses, men, and elephants then met an utterly merciless battle; and others, being struck down by the arrows, fled in terror.

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣāṃ tadā yuddhe saṃsaktānāṃ jayaiṣiṇām girim astaṃ samāsādya pratyapadyata bhānumān
english: While they were thus locked together in battle, longing for victory, the sun reached the western mountain and went to its setting.

sanskrit: tamasā ca mahārāja rajasā ca viśeṣataḥ na kiṃ cit pratyapaśyāma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
english: Then, great king, by reason of the darkness and especially of the dust, we could make out nothing at all, whether fair or foul.

sanskrit: te trasanto maheṣvāsā rātriyuddhasya bhārata apayānaṃ tataś cakruḥ sahitāḥ sarvavājibhiḥ
english: Those mighty bowmen, O Bhārata, dreading a battle by night, then drew off in a body together with all their horses.

sanskrit: kauraveṣu ca yāteṣu tadā rājan dinakṣaye jayaṃ sumanasaḥ prāpya pārthāḥ svaśibiraṃ yayuḥ
english: And when the Kauravas had withdrawn at the day's close, O king, the sons of Pṛthā, joyful at heart at having won the victory, went off to their own camp.

sanskrit: vāditraśabdair vividhaiḥ siṃhanādaiś ca nartitaiḥ parān avahasantaś ca stuvantaś cācyutārjunau
english: They went with the sounds of manifold instruments and with lion-roars and dancing, mocking their foes and extolling Acyuta and Arjuna.

sanskrit: kṛte 'vahāre tair vīraiḥ sainikāḥ sarva eva te āśiṣaḥ pāṇḍaveyeṣu prāyujyanta nareśvarāḥ
english: When the withdrawal had been made by those heroes, all the soldiers, those lords of men, pronounced their blessings upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛte 'vahāre ca prahṛṣṭāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ niśāyāṃ śibiraṃ gatvā nyaviśanta nareśvarāḥ
english: Then, the withdrawal accomplished, the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, those lords of men, well pleased, went to their encampments in the night and took their rest.

sanskrit: yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācāś ca śvāpadāni ca saṃghaśaḥ jagmur āyodhanaṃ ghoraṃ rudrasyānartanopamam
english: And Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Piśācas, and beasts of prey in throngs, repaired to that dreadful battlefield, which resembled the dancing-ground of Rudra.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca svena cchandena naḥ sarvān nāvadhīd vyaktam arjunaḥ na hy asya samare mucyetāntako 'py ātatāyinaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: It is plain that Arjuna did not slay us all only by his own choosing; for in battle not even Death himself, were he the aggressor, could escape him.

sanskrit: pārtho hy eko 'harad bhadrām ekaś cāgnim atarpayat ekaś cemāṃ mahīṃ jitvā cakre balibhṛto nṛpān
english: For Pṛthā's son alone carried off Bhadrā, alone he sated Agni, and alone, having conquered this earth, he made its kings bearers of tribute.

sanskrit: eko nivātakavacān avadhīd divyakārmukaḥ ekaḥ kirātarūpeṇa sthitaṃ śarvam ayodhayat
english: Alone, wielding his divine bow, he slew the Nivātakavacas; alone he fought against Śarva, who stood there in the guise of a Kirāta.

sanskrit: eko 'bhyarakṣad bharatān eko bhavam atoṣayat tenaikena jitāḥ sarve madīyā ugratejasaḥ te na nindyāḥ praśasyāś ca yat te cakrur bravīhi tat
english: Alone he protected the Bharatas, alone he pleased Bhava. By him alone were all my men of fierce energy vanquished. They are not to be blamed but rather praised. Tell me what it was they did.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hataprahatavidhvastā vivarmāyudhavāhanāḥ dīnasvarā dūyamānā māninaḥ śatrubhir jitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Slain, smitten, and shattered, stripped of their armor, weapons, and mounts, their voices pitiful and their hearts seared, those proud warriors had been overcome by their foes.

sanskrit: śibirasthāḥ punar mantraṃ mantrayanti sma kauravāḥ bhagnadaṃṣṭrā hataviṣāḥ padākrāntā ivoragāḥ
english: Within their camp the Kauravas once more took counsel together, like serpents whose fangs are broken, whose venom is gone, and who lie trodden underfoot.

sanskrit: tān abravīt tataḥ karṇaḥ kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan karaṃ kareṇābhipīḍya prekṣamāṇas tavātmajam
english: Then Karṇa, hissing like an enraged serpent, wringing one hand with the other and gazing at your son, spoke to them.

sanskrit: yatto dṛḍhaś ca dakṣaś ca dhṛtimān arjunaḥ sadā sa bodhayati cāpy enaṃ prāptakālam adhokṣajaḥ
english: Arjuna is ever vigilant, steadfast, skilled, and resolute; and Adhokṣaja besides keeps rousing him whenever the moment has come.

sanskrit: sahasāstravisargeṇa vayaṃ tenādya vañcitāḥ śvas tv ahaṃ tasya saṃkalpaṃ sarvaṃ hantā mahīpate
english: By his sudden release of missiles we have today been outwitted; but tomorrow, O lord of earth, I shall undo his every resolve.

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety uktvā so 'nujajñe nṛpottamān sukhoṣitās te rajanīṃ hṛṣṭā yuddhāya niryayuḥ
english: Addressed thus, the king said "So be it," and gave the foremost of princes leave to depart. Having passed the night in comfort, they set forth gladly for battle.

sanskrit: te 'paśyan vihitaṃ vyūhaṃ dharmarājena durjayam prayatnāt kurumukhyena bṛhaspatyuśanomatāt
english: They beheld the unassailable array drawn up with care by the Dharma King, that chief of the Kurus, after the doctrine of Bṛhaspati and Uśanas.

sanskrit: atha pratīpakartāraṃ satataṃ vijitātmanām sasmāra vṛṣabhaskandhaṃ karṇaṃ duryodhanas tadā
english: Then Duryodhana called to mind Karṇa, the bull-shouldered, the constant adversary of those who had mastered themselves.

sanskrit: puraṃdarasamaṃ yuddhe marudgaṇasamaṃ bale kārtavīryasamaṃ vīrye karṇaṃ rājño 'gaman manaḥ sūtaputraṃ maheṣvāsaṃ bandhum ātyayikeṣv iva
english: The king's mind turned to Karṇa, the equal of Purandara in battle, of the host of the Maruts in strength, and of Kārtavīrya in valor — the charioteer's son, that mighty bowman, like a kinsman in times of peril.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yad vo 'gaman mano mandāḥ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ tadā apy adrākṣata taṃ yūyaṃ śītārtā iva bhāskaram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Since your minds then turned to Karṇa Vaikartana, O dull-witted ones, did you look to him as men tormented by cold look to the sun?

sanskrit: kṛte 'vahāre sainyānāṃ pravṛtte ca raṇe punaḥ kathaṃ vaikartanaḥ karṇas tatrāyudhyata saṃjaya kathaṃ ca pāṇḍavāḥ sarve yuyudhus tatra sūtajam
english: When the withdrawal of the armies was over and battle was joined once more, how did Karṇa Vaikartana fight there, Saṃjaya, and how did all the Pāṇḍavas fight against the charioteer's son?

sanskrit: karṇo hy eko mahābāhur hanyāt pārthān sasomakān karṇasya bhujayor vīryaṃ śakraviṣṇusamaṃ matam tathāstrāṇi sughorāṇi vikramaś ca mahātmanaḥ
english: For the mighty-armed Karṇa alone could slay the sons of Pṛthā together with the Somakas. The strength of Karṇa's arms is held equal to that of Śakra and Viṣṇu, and so too are the most terrible weapons and the prowess of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavena bhṛśārditam parākrāntān pāṇḍusutān dṛṣṭvā cāpi mahāhave
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing then Duryodhana sorely afflicted by the Pāṇḍava, and seeing too the sons of Pāṇḍu prevailing in that great battle —

sanskrit: karṇam āśritya saṃgrāme darpo duryodhane punaḥ jetum utsahate pārthān saputrān sahakeśavān
english: — relying upon Karṇa in the fray, pride rose again in Duryodhana, and he dared to think he could conquer the sons of Pṛthā along with their sons and with Keśava.

sanskrit: aho bata mahad duḥkhaṃ yatra pāṇḍusutān raṇe nātarad rabhasaḥ karṇo daivaṃ nūnaṃ parāyaṇam aho dyūtasya niṣṭheyaṃ ghorā saṃprati vartate
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Alas, what great sorrow, that the impetuous Karṇa could not overcome the sons of Pāṇḍu in battle! Surely fate is the supreme refuge. Alas, this dreadful consummation of the dicing now comes to pass.

sanskrit: aho duḥkhāni tīvrāṇi duryodhanakṛtāny aham sahiṣyāmi sughorāṇi śalyabhūtāni saṃjaya
english: Alas, the sharp griefs wrought by Duryodhana — most terrible, like barbs in the flesh — these, Saṃjaya, I must endure.

sanskrit: saubalaṃ ca tathā tāta nītimān iti manyate
english: And the son of Subala too, my son, he reckons a man of sound policy.

sanskrit: yuddheṣu nāma divyeṣu vartamāneṣu saṃjaya aśrauṣaṃ nihatān putrān nityam eva ca nirjitān
english: While battles fit for the gods were going forward, Saṃjaya, I have heard ever and again of my sons being slain and overcome.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍavānāṃ samare kaś cid asti nivārakaḥ strīmadhyam iva gāhanti daivaṃ hi balavattaram
english: In battle there is none to hold the Pāṇḍavas back; they plunge into our ranks as into a throng of women, for fate is the stronger force.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atikrāntaṃ hi yat kāryaṃ paścāc cintayatīti ca tac cāsya na bhavet kāryaṃ cintayā ca vinaśyati
english: Saṃjaya said: He who broods afterward upon a deed already past — that deed of his is not undone thereby, and he himself is ruined by his grieving.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ tava kāryaṃ tu dūraprāptaṃ vijānatā na kṛtaṃ yat tvayā pūrvaṃ prāptāprāptavicāraṇe
english: This matter of yours has gone far indeed, for though you knew, you did not do beforehand what should have been done in weighing the possible against the impossible.

sanskrit: ukto 'si bahudhā rājan mā yudhyasveti pāṇḍavaiḥ gṛhṇīṣe na ca tan mohāt pāṇḍaveṣu viśāṃ pate
english: Many times, O king, you were told by the Pāṇḍavas, "Do not make war"; yet out of folly toward the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of peoples, you would not heed it.

sanskrit: tvayā pāpāni ghorāṇi samācīrṇāni pāṇḍuṣu tvatkṛte vartate ghoraḥ pārthivānāṃ janakṣayaḥ
english: Dreadful wrongs were committed by you against the sons of Pāṇḍu; and because of you this fearful destruction of the kings' folk comes to pass.

sanskrit: tat tv idānīm atikramya mā śuco bharatarṣabha śṛṇu sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ ghoraṃ vaiśasam acyuta
english: But now let that be past; grieve not, O bull of the Bharatas. Hear all the dreadful carnage just as it befell, O steadfast one.

sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu karṇo rājānam abhyayāt sametya ca mahābāhur duryodhanam abhāṣata
english: When night had brightened into dawn, Karṇa went to the king; and the mighty-armed one, drawing near, addressed Duryodhana.

sanskrit: adya rājan sameṣyāmi pāṇḍavena yaśasvinā haniṣyāmi ca taṃ vīraṃ sa vā māṃ nihaniṣyati
english: Today, O king, I shall meet the glorious Pāṇḍava, and I shall slay that hero — or he shall slay me.

sanskrit: bahutvān mama kāryāṇāṃ tathā pārthasya pārthiva nābhūt samāgamo rājan mama caivārjunasya ca
english: Owing to the multitude of my tasks and of Pṛthā's son's likewise, O king, no encounter has yet come about between me and Arjuna.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu me yathāprajñaṃ śṛṇu vākyaṃ viśāṃ pate anihatya raṇe pārthaṃ nāham eṣyāmi bhārata
english: But hear this word of mine, spoken to the best of my judgment, O lord of peoples: I shall not return from the field, O Bhārata, without having slain Pṛthā's son in battle.

sanskrit: hatapravīre sainye 'smin mayi caiva sthite yudhi abhiyāsyati māṃ pārthaḥ śakraśaktyā vinākṛtam
english: When the chief warriors of this host have fallen, and I alone stand fast in the fight, Pṛthā's son will come against me, who shall then be deprived of Śakra's dart.

sanskrit: tataḥ śreyaskaraṃ yat te tan nibodha janeśvara āyudhānāṃ ca yad vīryaṃ dravyāṇām arjunasya ca
english: Now learn, O ruler of men, what is most to your advantage, and the power of Arjuna's weapons and his equipment.

sanskrit: kāyasya mahato bhede lāghave dūrapātane sauṣṭhave cāstrayoge ca savyasācī na matsamaḥ
english: In cleaving a mighty frame, in nimbleness, in striking at a distance, in deftness, and in the wielding of missiles, Savyasācin is not my equal.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhamahāmātraṃ vijayaṃ nāma tad dhanuḥ indrārtham abhikāmena nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: There is that bow named Vijaya, surpassing all weapons, fashioned by Viśvakarman with great care for Indra's sake.

sanskrit: yena daityagaṇān rājañ jitavān vai śatakratuḥ yasya ghoṣeṇa daityānāṃ vimuhyanti diśo daśa tad bhārgavāya prāyacchac chakraḥ paramasaṃmatam
english: With it, O king, the Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices conquered the hosts of the Daityas; at its twang the ten quarters grew confused before the Daityas. That most prized bow Śakra bestowed upon the Bhārgava.

sanskrit: tad divyaṃ bhārgavo mahyam adadād dhanur uttamam yena yotsye mahābāhum arjunaṃ jayatāṃ varam yathendraḥ samare sarvān daiteyān vai samāgatān
english: That celestial, peerless bow the Bhārgava gave to me — with it I shall fight the mighty-armed Arjuna, foremost of the victorious, as Indra in battle fought all the assembled sons of Diti.

sanskrit: dhanur ghoraṃ rāmadattaṃ gāṇḍīvāt tad viśiṣyate triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī dhanuṣā tena nirjitā
english: This dreadful bow given by Rāma surpasses the Gāṇḍīva; thrice seven times was the earth conquered with that bow.

sanskrit: dhanuṣo yasya karmāṇi divyāni prāha bhārgavaḥ tad rāmo hy adadān mahyaṃ yena yotsyāmi pāṇḍavam
english: The bow whose celestial deeds the Bhārgava told of — that bow Rāma indeed gave to me, and with it I shall fight the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: adya duryodhanāhaṃ tvāṃ nandayiṣye sabāndhavam nihatya samare vīram arjunaṃ jayatāṃ varam
english: This day, Duryodhana, I shall gladden you and your kinsmen by slaying in battle the hero Arjuna, foremost of the victorious.

sanskrit: saparvatavanadvīpā hatadviḍ bhūḥ sasāgarā putrapautrapratiṣṭhā te bhaviṣyaty adya pārthiva
english: With its mountains, forests, and islands, with its seas, the earth, its foes slain, shall this day become an abode for your sons and grandsons, O king.

sanskrit: nāsādhyaṃ vidyate me 'dya tvatpriyārthaṃ viśeṣataḥ samyag dharmānuraktasya siddhir ātmavato yathā
english: Nothing is unattainable for me this day, above all for your dear sake — even as success belongs to the self-possessed man who cleaves rightly to dharma.

sanskrit: na hi māṃ samare soḍhuṃ sa śakto 'gniṃ tarur yathā avaśyaṃ tu mayā vācyaṃ yena hīno 'smi phalgunāt
english: For he can no more withstand me in battle than a tree can withstand fire. Yet I must needs declare wherein I fall short of Phalguna.

sanskrit: jyā tasya dhanuṣo divyā tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī tasya divyaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ gāṇḍīvam ajaraṃ yudhi
english: Divine is the string of his bow, and inexhaustible his two great quivers; his celestial bow, the matchless Gāṇḍīva, is undecaying in battle.

sanskrit: vijayaṃ ca mahad divyaṃ mamāpi dhanur uttamam tatrāham adhikaḥ pārthād dhanuṣā tena pārthiva
english: Yet I too have the great and celestial Vijaya, a most excellent bow; therein, by that bow, I surpass Pṛthā's son, O king.

sanskrit: mayā cābhyadhiko vīraḥ pāṇḍavas tan nibodha me raśmigrāhaś ca dāśārhaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ
english: But learn from me wherein the Pāṇḍava hero is greater than I: the holder of his reins is the Dāśārha, honored by all the worlds.

sanskrit: agnidattaś ca vai divyo rathaḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaḥ acchedyaḥ sarvato vīra vājinaś ca manojavāḥ dhvajaś ca divyo dyutimān vānaro vismayaṃkaraḥ
english: And his is the celestial chariot given by Agni, adorned with gold, indestructible on every side, O hero, and his steeds are swift as thought; and his banner is divine and shining — the wondrous ape.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaś ca sraṣṭā jagato rathaṃ tam abhirakṣati ebhir dravyair ahaṃ hīno yoddhum icchāmi pāṇḍavam
english: And Kṛṣṇa, the Maker of the world, guards that chariot. Wanting in these things, I yet wish to fight the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu sadṛśo vīraḥ śalyaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ sārathyaṃ yadi me kuryād dhruvas te vijayo bhavet
english: But here is a hero his match, Śalya, the ornament of the assembly: if he would act as my charioteer, your victory would be assured.

sanskrit: tasya me sārathiḥ śalyo bhavatv asukaraḥ paraiḥ nārācān gārdhrapatrāṃś ca śakaṭāni vahantu me
english: Let Śalya, hard for foes to overcome, become my charioteer; and let wagons carry my iron shafts fletched with vulture feathers.

sanskrit: rathāś ca mukhyā rājendra yuktā vājibhir uttamaiḥ āyāntu paścāt satataṃ mām eva bharatarṣabha
english: And let chief chariots, O lord of kings, yoked with the finest horses, follow ever close behind me, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: evam abhyadhikaḥ pārthād bhaviṣyāmi guṇair aham śalyo hy abhyadhikaḥ kṛṣṇād arjunād adhiko hy aham
english: Thus shall I surpass Pṛthā's son in advantages; for Śalya excels Kṛṣṇa, even as I excel Arjuna.

sanskrit: yathāśvahṛdayaṃ veda dāśārhaḥ paravīrahā tathā śalyo 'pi jānīte hayānāṃ vai mahārathaḥ
english: As the Dāśārha, slayer of hostile heroes, knows the heart of horses, so too does the great chariot-warrior Śalya understand them.

sanskrit: bāhuvīrye samo nāsti madrarājasya kaś cana tathāstrair matsamo nāsti kaś cid eva dhanurdharaḥ
english: In strength of arm none is the equal of the king of the Madras; and in weapons no bowman is the equal of me.

sanskrit: tathā śalyasamo nāsti hayayāne ha kaś cana so 'yam abhyadhikaḥ pārthād bhaviṣyati ratho mama
english: And in the driving of horses none here is the equal of Śalya. Thus this chariot of mine shall be superior to Pṛthā's son's.

sanskrit: etat kṛtaṃ mahārāja tvayecchāmi paraṃtapa evaṃ kṛte kṛtaṃ mahyaṃ sarvakāmair bhaviṣyati
english: This I wish done by you, O great king, scorcher of foes; when it is so done, my every desire will be fulfilled.

sanskrit: tato draṣṭāsi samare yat kariṣyāmi bhārata sarvathā pāṇḍavān sarvāñ jeṣyāmy adya samāgatān
english: Then you shall see in battle what I will do, O Bhārata: by every means I shall this day conquer all the Pāṇḍavas assembled against me.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca sarvam etat kariṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ karṇa manyase sopāsaṅgā rathāḥ sāśvā anuyāsyanti sūtaja
english: Duryodhana said: All this I shall do as you deem fit, Karṇa. Chariots with their quivers and horses shall follow after you, O son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: nārācān gārdhrapakṣāṃś ca śakaṭāni vahantu te anuyāsyāma karṇa tvāṃ vayaṃ sarve ca pārthivāḥ
english: And let wagons carry your iron shafts fletched with vulture feathers; and we and all the kings, Karṇa, will follow after you.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā mahārāja tava putrāḥ pratāpavān abhigamyābravīd rājā madrarājam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus, O great king, your majestic son the king drew near to the king of the Madras and addressed to him these words.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca putras tava mahārāja madrarājam idaṃ vacaḥ vinayenopasaṃgamya praṇayād vākyam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Your son, O great king, approaching the king of the Madras with humility, spoke to him this word out of affection.

sanskrit: satyavrata mahābhāga dviṣatām aghavardhana madreśvara raṇe śūra parasainyabhayaṃkara
english: O you whose vow is truth, O greatly fortunate one, increaser of the woes of your foes, O lord of the Madras, hero in battle, terror of the enemy host —

sanskrit: śrutavān asi karṇasya bruvato vadatāṃ vara yathā nṛpatisiṃhānāṃ madhye tvāṃ varayaty ayam
english: — you have heard Karṇa, O best of speakers, as he spoke, how in the midst of these lions among kings he chooses you.

sanskrit: tasmāt pārthavināśārthaṃ hitārthaṃ mama caiva hi sārathyaṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭha sumanāḥ kartum arhasi
english: Therefore, for the destruction of Pṛthā's son and indeed for my own good, O best of chariot-warriors, you should graciously consent to act as his charioteer.

sanskrit: asyābhīśugraho loke nānyo 'sti bhavatā samaḥ sa pātu sarvataḥ karṇaṃ bhavān brahmeva śaṃkaram
english: In all the world there is no holder of his reins to equal you. Guard Karṇa, then, on every side, as Brahmā guards Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: pārthasya sacivaḥ kṛṣṇo yathābhīśugraho varaḥ tathā tvam api rādheyaṃ sarvataḥ paripālaya
english: As Kṛṣṇa, the excellent holder of the reins, is the companion of Pṛthā's son, so do you too guard Rādheya on every side.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇo bhavān bhojaś ca vīryavān śakuniḥ saubalo drauṇir aham eva ca no balam eṣām eva kṛto bhāgo navadhā pṛtanāpate
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, yourself, the valiant Bhoja, Śakuni the son of Subala, the son of Droṇa, and I myself — these are our strength; and among these alone, O lord of the host, was the army apportioned in nine parts.
